regime.summary: SBP held at 10.5% on 2026-03-09 but the 6M bill cutoff is 1.00pp above the policy rate, so the curve prices hikes. CPI is rising and Brent is up 90.7% in three months. KSE100 is down 8.8% in a month and foreigners are net sellers. This resembles tightening plus external stress; the index is not yet in a confirmed bottom.

evidence.quote: Policy rate 10.5%; last MPC decision 2026-03-09: hold (+0bp)
Regime: 6M T-bill minus policy rate +1.00pp (market pricing hikes); CPI rising over 3 months (+0.8pp)
Tightening plus external stress: rate up 800bp in ten months with CPI above it.

core.thesis: Largest relative strength in the pack: 12m +109.1%, near its 252-day high, P/E 4.2, while the market fell. A bank is rate-sensitive and foreigners sold banks, so this is a business bet needing the B-questions on growth and sponsor, which the bundle cannot answer.

evidence.quote: B13. Is it growing, not merely stable?

core.thesis: Holding company that rose 20.8% in three months and 3.8% in one month against a falling market, within 8.8% of its high. Diversified, so it is a resting place rather than a timing bet. YoY EPS is down 16.6%, which I weigh against strength.

The oil link I hold: gas and oil producer with EPS up 14.4% YoY, flat over one month while the market fell, with Brent up 90.7%. Material information filed 2026-03-24 whose content the bundle does not give.

watch.subject: Next SBP MPC
watch.trigger: A hold with the 6M bill cutoff falling back toward 10.5% means hike pricing is fading: lift exposure toward the 75% default. A hike or a wider bill gap keeps exposure low.

watch.subject: KSE100 index
watch.trigger: Enter only on a known trigger: a first up close after a bottom with Brent and the bill gap no longer widening; add to the core then, not on the fall itself.

watch.subject: FABL
watch.trigger: EPS up 95.3% YoY at P/E 3.1 while price is down 4% in a month; revisit if the next MPC holds and banks stop being sold by foreigners.

watch.subject: CRTM
watch.trigger: Watch only; do not buy. Five upper locks in 10 days after a 146.6% one-month run; the measured rule is not tradable.

exposure_reason: Default is the core at about 75%. I hold 60%, 15 points less, because Brent is up 90.7% in three months, the 6M bill is 1.00pp over the policy rate (hikes priced) and CPI is rising; the closest past regime, tightening plus external stress, saw the median liquid stock fall far. No entry because no known trigger exists and the measured base rates give no timing edge. This is not cash on a no-edge rule: the three core names rest on relative strength and business questions, and the 40% in reserve is for a confirmed trigger or a business that earns it.
not_known: Reserves, current account and IMF status are not in the bundle. Business quality, sponsor record and float for MEBL, ENGROH and MARI are not given; I selected on price strength, P/E and earnings only. The content of MARI's material information is unknown.
contamination_note: No knowledge of events after 2026-03-27 was used. base_rates.csv is flagged as measured through 2026-10-16, so I took only rough type-level odds from it and nothing about specific names or dates.
